S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.

subtypes.Eating Very Small Amounts: Eating only one or two bites a day or extremely small portions per meal.
subtypes.Skipping Meals: Intentionally skipping breakfast, lunch, or dinner.
subtypes.Exclusion of Specific Food Groups: Strictly avoiding specific food groups like carbohydrates or fats to prevent nutritional imbalance.
subtypes.Strict Calorie Restriction: Limiting daily caloric intake to an extremely low level.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.

subtypes.Continuous Weight Loss: A state where weight continues to decrease due to intentional restriction of intake.
subtypes.Insistence on Low Weight: Attempting to lose more weight or refusing to restore weight despite already being underweight.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.

subtypes.Fear of Weight Gain: Extreme fear and loathing of gaining weight or becoming fat.
subtypes.Fear of Specific Foods: Fear that eating high-calorie foods will immediately lead to weight gain.
subtypes.Obsession with Weight Gain: Compulsively checking the scale and becoming extremely anxious about even the slightest increase.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.

subtypes.Distorted Body Image: Perceiving one's body as much fatter than it actually is or perceiving specific parts as excessively large when looking in the mirror.
subtypes.Self-Worth Dependent on Weight: Judging whether one is a good or successful person solely based on weight or body shape.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.

subtypes.Denial of Medical Risk: Not admitting or dismissing the health risks caused by being underweight.
subtypes.Disregard of Symptoms: Not taking physical symptoms caused by low weight (dizziness, hair loss, amenorrhea) seriously.
subtypes.Dismissal of Concerns: Exaggerating or rejecting the concerns of doctors or family as unnecessary.

symptom.disease_info: Anorexia nervosa is defined by persistent restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, together with intense fear of weight gain and a disturbance in how body weight or shape is experienced or valued. Patients often minimize the medical seriousness of their low weight, and the course may become clinically evident through medical, family, occupational, or school-related concerns rather than through the patient’s own recognition. It is distinguished from other eating or weight-loss conditions by the combination of low weight, weight-gain fear, body-image overvaluation, and lack of appropriate concern about the weight loss.

patient.stressor: When Jaritza enrolled in evening GED classes with the hope of qualifying for a logistics coordinator track, her already irregular warehouse schedule became tightly packed between shifts, homework, softball, and food-bank volunteering. At first, she framed cutting back meals as a practical way to save time and stay disciplined for school, but over time the restriction became organized around feeling more in control and judging herself by changes in her body. Even after her weight fell well below what was healthy for her, she insisted that people in her church and hiking club were overreacting and that gaining weight would mean losing the progress she had worked for. She came to psychiatric care after a primary-care visit required for a warehouse wellness form led to a referral when her low weight and firm denial of its seriousness raised concern.

S043.name: Restrictive_Intake
S043.description: Persistent restriction of energy intake relative to requirements, leading to significantly low body weight.
S043.manifestation: I’m here because the clinic got on me about how little I’ve been eating, but most days I’m just grabbing coffee before the warehouse, maybe a yogurt or a few bites after GED class, because sitting down for a real meal feels like it throws off everything I’m trying to keep in line.

S044.name: Low_Weight
S044.description: A body weight that is significantly below the minimum level of health for age, sex, developmental trajectory, and physical health.
S044.manifestation: Even with my work pants loose and people saying I look too thin, when I see the number go down I feel like I’m finally getting somewhere, and I don’t see why I should be pushed to put it back on.

S045.name: Fear_of_Weight_Gain
S045.description: Intense fear of gaining weight or of becoming fat, even though at a significantly low weight.
S045.manifestation: If I eat something like fried food from the break room or a big plate at church, I get scared it’s going to show on me right away, so I’ll keep thinking about it and want to check the scale.

S046.name: Body_Image_Weight_Shape_Disturbance
S046.description: Undue influence of body weight or shape on self-evaluation.
S046.manifestation: When I look in the mirror before class or softball, my stomach and thighs still look bigger than they should, and it can make me feel like I’m either doing good or failing for the whole day.

S084.name: Low_Weight_Severity_Non_Recognition
S084.description: Persistent lack of recognition of the seriousness of the current low body weight.
S084.manifestation: I know the doctor and people from church are worried, but I honestly think they’re making it bigger than it is because I’m still going to work, doing my classes, and keeping up with my life.

add_requirements.functional_impairment: I’m still showing up for work and class, but I’ve been turning down meals after church and leaving GED homework unfinished because I’m so focused on keeping my eating and schedule controlled.
